page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two medallion portraits side by side with their legends. Below them, one column of running text with two paragraphs. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: IVGVRTHA, Micipsæ Numidarum regis adoptiuus hæ-res, Hiempsalis capite potitus, in Adherbalem se conuertit (hi erant fratres regni cohæredes.) Adherbal Romā profugit (nam in Romanorum fide ac clientela regnum Numidicū erat) missa itaque pecunia primò in sententiā suam senatum trahit Iugur-tha: deinde missis à senatu, qui regnum diuiderent, inchoatum nefas perficit, pacem emit. Accersitus posthæc Romā, publica interueniente fide, vbi venit, auro omnibus corruptis aut at-tentatis, omnia dissentionibus permiscet: discedénsque dicit, O Urbem venalem, & citò perituram, si emptorem inveniat. Placet deinde Senatui bello hunc parricidam persequi, Sp. Albinus in eum mittitur, cuius exercitū auro etiam corrumpit Iugurtha. Assurgit Metellus, qui eum duobus præliis vincit: cumque iam bello finé impositurus effet, successit C. Marius, qui Bocchum Mauritaniæ regem Iugurthæ socerum superat: Bocchus precium fœderis atque amicitiæ, regem Iugurtham facit: quem catenis opertum in triumpho populus Romanus aspexit. Eutr. li.4. Flo.li.3. Sall. Plutar. in Mar. & Syl. Romæ in scrobe demissus post sextum diem fame ac frigore atteritur, anno mundi 3857. ante Christum natum 105.

C. MARIVS cum Q. Catulo aduersus Cymbros missus, victoriam reportat, anno mundi 3863. ante Christum natum 99. Hic affectauit ut ad bellum Mithridaticū mitteretur: quare Sylla commotus, Marium urbe fugat: inde perniciosissimum bellum ciuile exortum. Eutr. li.5. Appi.li.1.ca.8. Flo.li.3.ca.3. fuit septies Consul: victus à Sylla, in palude latuit: in vincula inde coiectus, immissum percussorem, autoritate vultus terruit, & scapha in Africam traiecit: fertur voluntaria morte obiisse.

page.notes: Two medallion woodcuts at the top, not text. Left medal legend: "IVGVRTHA" on the right edge and "NVMIDAE REGI" partly visible on the left edge, only partly legible, read as "NVM[?] R[?]". Right medal legend: "C MARIVS" on the left edge and "COS VII" on the right edge. The printed "Eutr.", "Flo.", "Sall." and similar citations are in the running text. Doubtful readings: "NVM[?] R[?]" on the left medal, as the lettering is partly cut off. The printed text reads "permiscet" and "effet", as the scan shows, and these are kept as printed.
